entities.name: Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Karabakh
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Karabakh (Azerbaijani: Azərbaycan Dövlət Qarabağ Tarixi Muzeyi) in Shusha (Shushi), Karabakh — established after Azerbaijan recaptured Shusha in May 2020 and subsequently all of Nagorno-Karabakh in September 2023 — is an official Azerbaijani cultural institution presenting the Azerbaijani historical narrative of Karabakh as an integral part of Azerbaijan's territorial and cultural heritage, directly counterpointing Armenian claims to the same territory.

Shusha (known to Armenians as Shushi) is one of the most symbolically contested cities in the South Caucasus: historically a significant Azerbaijani khanate capital and cultural center (described as the 'Conservatory of the Caucasus' for its musical traditions), it was majority-Armenian before 1920 and majority-Azerbaijani in the 18th-19th centuries. Shusha's capture in May 2020 (during the 44-Day War) was celebrated by Azerbaijan as the 'liberation' of its most culturally significant city; its loss was mourned by Armenians as the fall of a city they considered the 'cultural capital' of Artsakh.

The museum represents Azerbaijan's effort to institutionalize its historical narrative about Karabakh — presenting Azerbaijani khanate history, cultural heritage, and the Karabakh War from an Azerbaijani perspective. Its existence in Shusha alongside the reconstruction of Azerbaijani cultural sites (while Armenian churches face questions about their preservation status) reflects the broader cultural dimension of a post-conflict territorial reintegration.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Karabakh in Shusha — established after Azerbaijan's 2020-2023 military resolution of the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, institutionalizing the Azerbaijani historical narrative — is historically significant as a monument to the cultural dimension of one of the post-Soviet era's most intractable territorial conflicts.
